title: Marston Earth Load — Trench Condition

W_d.description: Earth load on pipe per unit length

B_d.description: Trench width at top of pipe

applicability: K = ratio of lateral to vertical pressure (Rankine: 0.33 for sand). μ' = coefficient of friction between fill and trench walls (tan φ, typically 0.3–0.5). Cd from tables/charts as function of H/Bd. For H/Bd > 10, Cd approaches 1/(2Kμ').

title: Marston Earth Load — Positive Projecting Embankment

W_c.description: Earth load on pipe per unit length (embankment)

C_c.description: Embankment load coefficient (function of H/D and settlement ratio rsd)

applicability: For pipe projecting above natural ground, buried under embankment fill. rsd > 0 (complete projection) gives Cc > H/D (load exceeds prism). rsd < 0 (settling pipe) gives Cc < H/D. For rigid pipe on rock foundation: rsd → +1.0, very high loads.

title: Prism Earth Load (Simplified)

γ.description: Unit weight of soil above pipe

H.description: Depth of cover above pipe crown

applicability: Simple overburden weight. Conservative for trench condition. May underestimate embankment loads on rigid pipe (due to negative arching). Commonly used for flexible pipe design as a reasonable approximation.

title: AASHTO Live Load on Buried Pipe

W_L.description: Live load on pipe per unit length

P.description: Wheel load (72 kN for HL-93 design truck)

C_s.description: Surface load distribution coefficient (function of H)

L_e.description: Effective length of load spread at pipe crown

applicability: Simplified approach. At H=0.6 m: WL is very significant. At H=2.4 m: WL approaches earth load magnitude. At H > 3 m: WL often negligible. AASHTO LRFD provides more detailed distribution factors.
source: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, AWWA C150

title: Modified Iowa Formula — Flexible Pipe Deflection

K.description: Bedding constant (0.1 for typical point/narrow bedding, 0.083–0.110)

W_c.description: Total vertical load per unit length (earth + live)

EI/r³.description: Pipe ring stiffness per unit length

applicability: Predicts ring deflection under load. Flexible pipe relies on E's (soil support) — proper haunch compaction is critical. For HDPE: EI decreases with time due to creep — use long-term modulus.

title: Pipe Ring Stiffness

E.description: Modulus of elasticity of pipe material

I.description: Moment of inertia of pipe wall per unit length = t³/12

applicability: Measure of pipe's inherent ring bending resistance. For flexible pipe, PS is much less than 0.061E's — soil provides most of the support. ASTM D2412 defines pipe stiffness at 5% deflection (F/Δy test).

title: Buckling Pressure — Buried Flexible Pipe

EI.description: Pipe wall stiffness per unit length

applicability: Safety factor ≥ 2.0 against buckling. External pressure = groundwater + vacuum (if any). Buckling is interactive with deflection — heavily deflected pipe buckles at lower pressure.

title: Rigid Pipe — Required D-Load

W_total.description: Total load per unit length (earth + live + safety factor)

B_f.description: Bedding factor (1.1–4.8 depending on installation type)

applicability: Select pipe class (ASTM C76 for RCP) with D-load strength ≥ D_load_req. Factor of safety of 1.0 is typically applied to the 0.3mm crack D-load (D_0.3), or 1.5 to the ultimate D-load.

title: Flexible Pipe — Combined Loading Check
equation: σ_wall = (σ_ring_bending)² + (σ_hoop)² - σ_ring × σ_hoop ≤ σ_allow²  (von Mises simplified)

σ_ring_bending.description: Bending stress from external load deflection

applicability: For flexible pipe under simultaneous internal pressure and external load. Ring bending stress = 4×E×t×Δx/(D²) for elastic ring. Most design standards check deflection and pressure separately rather than combined.

title: Transition Width (Trench to Embankment Loading)

B_d_transition.description: Trench width at which trench load equals embankment load

C_d_max.description: Maximum trench load coefficient (at large H/Bd)

applicability: For trench widths wider than the transition width, the pipe load is governed by embankment conditions regardless of the trench. Important for design — wider trenches do not always mean less load. AWWA C150 provides transition width tables.
